extracted.intended_audience: readers and prospective contributors to The Spectator; general literate public; playwrights and writers on trade
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for contributors to The Spectator (periodical essays), with adjacent prescriptive remarks about theatrical writing and writings on trade — covering submission practice, content quality, moral aims, and reader value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish submissions entire and without alteration
rubrics_metrics.description: I am resolved for the Future to publish any 'Spectator' that deserves it, entire, and without any Alteration; assuring the World (if there can be Need of it) that it is none of mine and if the Authors think fit to subscribe their Names, I will add them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor previously 'dressed' contributors into his own style but now recognizes some papers should appear in 'their own native Dress and Colours'; will print contributions unaltered and will append authors' names only if they subscribe. Encourages fidelity to original voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open invitation to diverse contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: I will invite all manner of Persons, whether Scholars, Citizens, Courtiers, Gentlemen of the Town or Country, and all Beaux, Rakes, Smarts, Prudes, Coquets, Housewives, and all Sorts of Wits ... and of what Manners or Dispositions soever ... who have ever made Thinking a Part of their Business or Diversion, and have any thing worthy to impart on these Subjects to the World.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicits pieces from an extremely broad social range (all sexes, ages, professions, humours, conditions). The aim is to show different Thoughts and Observations in the clearest and most genuine Light; contributors should write according to their talents and circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to stated thesis within deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Thesis propos'd for the present Exercise of the Adventurers to write Spectators, is MONEY, on which Subject all Persons are desired to send their Thoughts within Ten Days after the Date hereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement: contributions on the announced subject should be submitted within the specified short timeframe (ten days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Each paper must give readers its price in value
rubrics_metrics.description: I would not advise any one to take it in, who after the Perusal of it, does not find himself Two-pence the wiser, or the better Man for it; or who upon Examination, does not believe that he has had Two-pennyworth of Mirth or Instruction for his Money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard of value: every issue should deliver tangible instruction or entertainment proportional to its cost — the reader should feel materially improved or amused by the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writings on trade must refrain from glorifying base methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Good Lectures to young Traders may have very good Effects on their Conduct: but beware you propagate no false Notions of Trade; let none of your Correspondents impose on the World, by putting forth base Methods in a good Light, and glazing them over with improper Terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice for essays about commerce: present only laudable methods of profit; do not call 'Noise' industry, nor 'Impudence' courage; don't mistake good Fortune for good Management; distinguish niggardliness from good husbandry and generosity from profusion. Use moral exemplars (e.g., Honestus vs Fortunatus) to contrast honest trade with imposture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors should practise humility about their own performances
rubrics_metrics.description: An Author should take all Methods to humble himself in the Opinion he has of his own Performances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitative norm for writers: maintain modesty about one's work, be open to others' contributions, and avoid vanity that would exclude worthy papers by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on ostentation to establish credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: There is something unaccountably taking among the Vulgar in those who come from a great Way off ... The Art of managing Mankind, is only to make them stare a little, to keep up their Astonishment; ... I keep a Latin Sentence in my Front; and I was not a little pleased when I observed one of my Readers say, 'More Latin still? What a prodigious Scholar is this Man!'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical observation and implied guideline: ostentatious trappings (foreign travel, Latin, curiosities, sensational claims) can create false credibility; writers and practitioners should avoid relying on superficial signs to impress or deceive an audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatre should be virtuous and advance morality
rubrics_metrics.description: Were our English Stage but half so virtuous as that of the Greeks or Romans, we should quickly see the Influence of it in the Behaviour of all the Politer Part of Mankind. ... It would not be fashionable to ridicule Religion, or its Professors; the Man of Pleasure would not be the compleat Gentleman; Vanity would be out of Countenance...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative standard for plays: the stage ought to contribute to the advancement of morality and the reformation of the age; it should refine human nature and make audiences 'wiser and better' after viewing. Suggests inspections/limitations to restrain licentiousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent vices so they are not attractive; avoid improper subjects for ridicule
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever Vices are represented upon the Stage, they ought to be so marked and branded by the Poet, as not to appear either laudable or amiable in the Person who is tainted with them. ... Now a Subject is improper for Ridicule, if it is apt to stir up Horrour and Commiseration rather than Laughter. For this Reason, we do not find any Comedy in so polite an Author as Terence, raised upon the Violations of the Marriage-Bed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dramatic-ethical criteria: (1) ensure that immoral characters are clearly censured so vice is not admired; (2) avoid ridiculing subjects that naturally provoke horror or compassion (e.g., sexual violation, tragic suffering); (3) distinguish legitimate comic targets from improper ones; do not mistake mere bawdiness for wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish genuine wit from lewd or vulgar humour
rubrics_metrics.description: When Persons of a low Genius attempt this kind of Writing, they know no difference between being Merry and being Lewd. ... It is one of the most unaccountable things in our Age, that the Lewdness of our Theatre should be so much complained of, so well exposed, and so little redressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetic criterion for comedy and comic writing: true wit should not rely on lewdness or gross strokes; avoid pandering to a vicious taste of the audience and instead aim for humour that corrects or exposes immoral conduct rather than celebrating it.
